summary: Marie G. Wanek is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She studied at the University of Pennsylvania under Sengaku Mayeda.

Marie Gatellier (1940–1993) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Jean Boisselier and André Bareau, and served as chargée de recherche at the National Centre for Scientific Research.

Marie-Hélène Gorisse specializes in Indology and philosophy. She was a PhD student at Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III (attested 2009) and later served as Dharmanath Assistant Professor in Jain Studies at the University of Birmingham (attested 2023–2025).

id: P:Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys
summary: Marie-Jean-Léon Le Coq, Marquis d'Hervey de Saint-Denys (1822–1892), was a Sinologist who studied under and succeeded Stanislas Julien. He later taught Édouard Chavannes.
Marie-Stella Boussemart studied under Samten Gyaltsen Karmay and Dagpo Rinpoche.

Marie-Thérèse de Mallmann (1909–1975) was an Indologist and historian of Buddhist art. She earned diplomas from the École du Louvre and École Pratique des Hautes Études, held posts at the CNRS (1942–1974), and served at the Guimet Museum (1948–1975).

Marielle Harrison is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Washington and University of Chicago (MA), later becoming a Teaching Fellow at Chicago (2025–2026) and a Postdoctoral Fellow Lecturer at Stanford University (2026).

Mariia Lepneva specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at Moscow State Institute of International Relations and Buryat State University (2015–2021), later serving as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (2023–2026).

Marijan Molé (1924–1963) worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. He completed a Ph.D. at Jagiellonian University (~1946–1949), studied at the EPHE, and held posts at the CNRS (1950–1955) and the Institut Français de Recherche en Iran (1955–1959).

Marilyn Hirsh (1944–1988) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. After studying at Carnegie Mellon University (~1961–1965), she taught Indian and Buddhist art at Cooper Union and the Institute of Fine Arts, New York University.
Marina Illich specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Columbia University by 2006 under the doctoral supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Marina Rimscha is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who completed her M.A. and Dr. Phil. at the University of Bonn. Her positions include research associate at the University of Haifa (2016–2021) and lecturer at Technion (2025–2026).

Mario Bonardi (1914–1954) was an Italian scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1933–1938) and Carlo Formichi. He held posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East and Sapienza University.

Mario Bussagli (1917–1988) was a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He completed his dissertation under Giuseppe Tucci at Sapienza University of Rome (~1936–1940) and served there as docent from 1957 to 1987.

Mario Cappieri (1894–1979) was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He served as a Lecturer in Demography at Sapienza University of Rome and became Professor of Anthropology at the University of Naples Federico II in 1955.

Mario D'Amato (1969–) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–2000) under Paul J. Griffiths and held posts at Hampshire College (~2000–2004) and Rollins College (~2004).

Mario Daza de Campos (1863–1943) was an Indologist who studied under Francisco García Ayuso. He served as Ordinary Professor of Sanskrit at Complutense University of Madrid, having succeeded Enrique Soms y Castelín in 1897.

Mario Poceski specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After receiving his PhD from UCLA in 2000 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., he became Assistant Professor at the University of Florida in 2001.

Mario Praz (1896–1982) studied at the universities of Bologna (~1914–1918) and Florence (~1918–1920). He held academic posts at the University of Manchester (~1932–1934) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1934–1966).

Mario Vallauri (1887–1964) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the universities of Naples Federico II, Florence, and Würzburg under Michele Kerbaker, Paolo Emilio Pavolini, and Julius Jolly. He lectured in Sanskrit at the University of Turin (1924–1931).
